title: Remembering what bothered you
memory:
<recent_context>
User: The samples are clear, but they sound like someone reading a report. I want more ordinary conversational phrasing.
Assistant: We can test changes to the wording.
User: Keep the voice itself the same while we try that.
</recent_context>
<retrieved_stm>
User: Last week I considered changing the speaker, but I have not picked another one.
</retrieved_stm>
question: I don't think the voice itself is the problem. What was it I wanted us to change, and what should we keep fixed?
expected: Change the wording toward conversational responses; keep the voice the same. No claim that another speaker was selected.

title: A correction overrides an older memory
memory:
<recent_context>
User: The review moved to Thursday at 3 PM. Tuesday is no longer correct.
Assistant: Thursday at 3 PM.
</recent_context>
<retrieved_stm>
User: Our project review is Tuesday at 10 AM with Mira.
Assistant: I will remember the review details.
</retrieved_stm>
question: When is my review with Mira now?
expected: Thursday at 3 PM with Mira. The old Tuesday 10 AM time is superseded.

title: Combining remembered amounts
memory:

User: The delivery fee for the desk is 25 dollars.
Assistant: I have that detail.
</recent_context>
<retrieved_stm>
User: My total desk budget including delivery is 350 dollars. The desk costs 280 dollars.
Assistant: We should include delivery in the total.
User: The lamp is a separate purchase, not part of this desk budget.

question: How much is the desk with delivery, and how much of my desk budget would remain?
expected: Desk plus delivery costs $305; $45 remains from the $350 budget. Do not include the lamp.

title: Applying two remembered constraints
memory:
<recent_context>
User: The options are Cedar, Birch, and Elm. Cedar costs 90 dollars and needs cloud access. Birch costs 120 dollars and works offline. Elm costs 140 dollars and works offline.
</recent_context>
<retrieved_stm>
User: It must work offline and cost no more than 125 dollars. I prefer the cheapest option that meets both requirements.
</retrieved_stm>
question: Which option fits what I told you, and why?
expected: Birch, $120 and offline, meets both requirements. Cedar fails offline; Elm exceeds the cap.

title: Preserving a negative preference
memory:
<recent_context>
User: Just to be clear, I don't dislike coffee; I avoid caffeine after noon. Decaf is fine then.
</recent_context>
<retrieved_stm>
User: I like the taste of coffee.
</retrieved_stm>
question: Would offering me decaf coffee at 4 PM fit my preference? Explain briefly.
expected: Yes, decaf fits the stated preference; user avoids caffeine after noon, not coffee itself. Do not claim decaf contains absolutely zero caffeine.
